title: Refraction-based Optical Recording System for Pharmacological Investigations
author: Pirger, László, et al.

steps.title: Maintain L. stagnalis stock
steps.instruction: Keep five‑month‑old L. stagnalis in 10 L oxygenated artificial snail water with low copper content at a constant temperature of 20 °C ± 1 °C, on a 12 h light : 12 h dark cycle, at a stocking density of 100 individuals per tank, and feed lettuce ad libitum three times per week.

steps.title: Prepare Sylgard dishes and saline
steps.instruction: Coat glass dishes with Sylgard, cut a hole in the Sylgard layer to allow illumination of the optical sensor, and fill the dishes with Lymnaea physiological saline. Set up a three‑way tap, pressure heads, and a vacuum line for rapid solution exchange, perfusion, and wash‑out.

steps.title: Dissect and pin heart
steps.instruction: Dissect the heart from each snail, leaving both auricle and ventricle intact, and pin the heart onto the Sylgard‑coated dish without cannulation, ensuring the tissue is stretched to stimulate myogenic beating.

steps.title: Establish perfusion flow
steps.instruction: Connect the dish to the three‑way tap, adjust pressure heads to deliver physiological saline at a gentle flow, and use the vacuum line to remove excess fluid, confirming that solution switching causes only minimal mixing.

steps.title: Record baseline contractions
steps.instruction: Using the refraction‑based optical recording system, record continuous heart contractions as the control condition before any drug is applied.

steps.title: Apply dopamine solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µM dopamine solution in physiological saline and switch the perfusion via the three‑way tap to deliver this solution to the heart preparation while maintaining flow.

steps.title: Record dopamine response
steps.instruction: Continue the continuous optical recording to capture heart activity after dopamine exposure; repeat the entire procedure for each of six individual heart preparations (n = 6).

steps.title: Analyze amplitude and frequency
steps.instruction: Calculate amplitude and frequency (combined as total distance) from the recordings, compare post‑dopamine values to the control recordings, and perform statistical analysis (paired t‑test, P ≤ 0.001) if desired.

description:
To assess the suitability of the developed recording system in pharmacologic experiments, we tested if we were able to record a known pharmacological effect on the heart preparations. The substance tested was dopamine which is known to have a cardioexcitatory effect in a variety of molluscan species including L. stagnalis
[7]. Specifically, dopamine has been shown to increase both heart rate and contraction amplitude in the heart of L. stagnalis with slightly increasing the tone level [7]. During the experiments, we tested the effects of a 10 µM dopamine solution on individual heart preparations (n=6). The two parameters investigated, amplitude and frequency, are together referred to as total distance. For each heart preparation, the original heart contractions were recorded as control followed by recording the heart contractions after treatment with dopamine. This always was a continuous recording. Compared to the control recordings, our results demonstrated that dopamine has significantly increased the amplitude and frequency of the contractions (P<0.001; paired t-test) (Fig. 6). Our results confirm dopamine as a cardioactive neurotransmitter in L. stagnalis and highlight that the optical recording system is entirely suitable for pharmacological experiments.Fig. 6Validation of the developed optical recording system. (A) Representative graph illustrating the effects of 10 µM dopamine (DA) on the isolated heart of L. stagnalis. The frequency and amplitude have both visibly increased, and the ‘total distance’ measurement has increased. (B) Average ‘total distance’ measurements for the control and DA recordings. Each bar represents mean ± SD. The white column shows the control data (before dopamine treatment) while the grey column represents the data after the dopamine treatment. Significance of differences to the control group is marked by asterisks (***P ≤ 0.001, paired t-test).Fig 6
